hero.title: Wildfire risk intelligence for rural communities
hero.subtitle: A geospatial platform for municipalities, civil protection and researchers to map, model and act on wildfire risk — turning local knowledge and data into proactive protection before the flames ignite.

challenge.title: Wildfires are no longer isolated disasters — they are a seasonal crisis
challenge.p1: Across Southern Europe, rising temperatures, longer droughts and unpredictable weather are turning forests into fuel. Rural depopulation means less land management and greater vegetation build-up, making outbreaks more intense and harder to control.
challenge.p2: Recent seasons in Portugal, Spain and Greece were among the worst on record — costing lives, destroying ecosystems and displacing communities, while threatening agriculture, forestry, tourism and basic safety. Local actors remain under-equipped and under-supported.

hotter.title: Hotter, drier seasons
hotter.text: Climate shifts extend the fire season year on year.

vegetation.title: Vegetation build-up
vegetation.text: Depopulation leaves landscapes unmanaged and fuel-rich.

cascading.title: Cascading impact
cascading.text: Ecosystems, economies and rural life are all at risk.

tooling.title: Limited tooling
tooling.text: Communities lack shared, data-driven decision support.

windSpeed.title: Wind Speed
windSpeed.description: Average wind speed over the selected area for the given time period.
windSpeed.example: Higher wind speeds provide more oxygen to the fire and can rapidly spread embers, significantly increasing the rate of fire spread.

windDirection.title: Wind Direction
windDirection.description: Average wind direction over the selected area, represented in degrees and compass points.
windDirection.example: N (North), E (East), S (South), W (West), and intermediate points like NNE (North-Northeast) or WSW (West-Southwest).

temperature.title: Temperature
temperature.description: Average ambient temperature over the selected area for the given time period.
temperature.example: High temperatures dry out vegetation (fuels), making them easier to ignite and allowing the fire to burn more intensely.

humidity.title: Relative Humidity
humidity.description: Average relative humidity over the selected area for the given time period.
humidity.example: Low relative humidity means the air is dry, which draws moisture out of the vegetation, creating highly flammable fuels.

layer1.staticHint: Static runs use one available weather date, from 16:00 to 17:00.
layer1.dynamicHint: Dynamic runs keep the selected date range and use the 16:00 to 17:00 window.
layer1.dynamicSelectInside: Select a range inside available dynamic dates: {{start}} to {{end}}
layer1.calcModeInfo: Static assesses a single day — one available weather date — using the AOI risk workflow. Dynamic assesses a range of days, keeping the daily weather sequence. Both use the 16:00–17:00 weather window.
layer1.calcModeHintStatic: The hottest day of each available year.
layer1.calcModeHintDynamic: A range of days, assessed day by day.
layer1.modelNameQuestion: What do you want to call this model?
layer1.calcModeQuestion: How should the risk be calculated?
layer1.calcModeStaticInfo: The date is picked for you: for each available year, the day that recorded the highest temperature — the worst-case weather for that year. Assessed from 16:00 to 17:00.
layer1.calcModeDynamicInfo: You choose the range and it is assessed exactly as selected: every day is modelled with its own weather and the run returns the peak-risk day. Each day uses the 16:00–17:00 window.

layer3.historicalHint: Recurrence based on past fire incidents in the area
layer3.weatherWarning: Fire-weather is the main risk signal. Disabling it makes the date selection irrelevant and produces a drastically under-estimated risk map. Keep it on unless you specifically need a baseline without weather.
layer3.customDataDesc: Bring your own weather inputs for this area. If left empty, the bundled regional data is used.
layer3.weatherStationInfo: Hourly weather measurements from a local station — temperature, humidity, wind and precipitation. Used to compute the Fire Weather Index for this area. Upload an Excel or CSV export; if omitted, the bundled regional weather data is used.
layer3.coreSignalsNote: Vegetation (NDVI) and infrastructure are always part of the model and cannot be switched off. Switching a signal above off removes its contribution from the weighting — the run continues with the remaining signals.
layer3.precomputedInfo: Every night the whole region is analysed with all risk layers enabled. When your date is covered, your area's result is clipped from that map and arrives in seconds. Disable it (or toggle individual layers below) to compute every step specifically for your area (~1-2 minutes).
layer3.precomputedOnHint: Result in seconds, clipped from tonight's whole-region analysis. All three risk layers below are included and therefore locked.
layer3.precomputedOffHint: Full computation for your exact area (~1-2 minutes); you can toggle individual layers below.
layer3.precomputedRange: Precomputed maps cover exactly one day - select the same start and end date to use one. For a date range the model computes every day for your area and returns the peak-risk day (~1-2 minutes).
layer3.precomputedStaticMode: Precomputed maps exist only for dynamic assessments. The model will compute all steps for your area.
layer3.precomputedUnavailable: The nightly analysis has not processed this date yet. The model will compute all steps for your area.
layer3.lockedByPrecomputed: Included in the precomputed regional map. Disable the precomputed switch above to customise layers.
layer3.signalsQuestion: Which signals should feed the risk model?
layer3.fwiInfo: The Fire Weather Index combines wind, relative humidity, temperature and drought into one measure of how readily a fire would start and spread. It carries the largest weight because weather changes fastest and drives fire behaviour most strongly.
layer3.terrainInfo: Slope, elevation and aspect shape how a fire moves: it accelerates uphill, and sun-facing slopes dry out faster. Derived from the digital terrain model for your area.
layer3.historicalInfo: Where fires have burned before they tend to burn again, because the underlying causes — land use, access and ignition sources — persist. Based on recorded past fire incidents in the area.

layer4.purpose: Real-time validation of the model configuration. Blockers must be cleared in their respective steps before the run can start.
layer4.nextStepHint: Then you'll save the model and kick off the calculation.
layer4.staticSingleDate: Static mode requires a single date.
layer4.staticNotInWindow: Date {{date}} is not in the available static dates window.
layer4.dynamicRequiresBefore: Dynamic mode requires start before end.
layer4.dynamicUnavailableDates: The selected dynamic date range contains unavailable dates.
layer4.noPolygon: No polygon drawn on the map.
layer4.weatherDisabledWarn: Fire-weather (FWI) is disabled — risk will be significantly under-estimated and the date becomes irrelevant.
layer4.allSignalsActive: All risk signals active (weather + terrain + history).
layer4.someSignalsActive: Running with {{count}} of 3 optional signals — output will differ from the full model.
layer4.allPassed: All checks passed. Ready to save & calculate.

layer5.purpose: Review the model setup before saving. The calculation will use the selected dates, area and data source choices.
layer5.dailyRunInfo: Every simulated day is assessed with the weather from this window — the hottest, driest part of the afternoon.

coverage.blankDesc: Blank areas have no valid source raster data for calculation.
